Ni Weide, from Kaifeng, moved to the Suzhou region at some unknown date. He was there in the 1320s looking for a teacher when he found books by Liu Wansu, Zhang Congzheng, and Li Gao. See Wu Yiyi 1993-94: 56-7, citing the Wu county gazetteer (1642; 53.24a-b), Wuzhong renwu zhi 吳中人物志 (1570), and Song Lian's "Gu Ni fujun muzhiming" 故倪府君墓誌銘 (Song Wenxian gong quanji 宋文憲公全集 25.5b-6a). $ ^{148} $ Hua was from Xiangcheng 襄城 (southwest of Kaifeng); he later moved to nearby Yizhen 儀真, and finally to Yuyao 餘姚 (northern Zhejiang, where Xiang Xin's family also lived, at the end of a canal connected to the Grand Canal). The data concerning Hua's moves comes from his biography in History of the Ming (299: 7634-35). Apart from the Basic Questions and the Canon of Problems that his master had made him read, Hua developed his doctrines and skills with the books of Zhang Ji, Liu Wansu, and Li Gao.
